column2: With Mr. Kobayashi at the center, we all stood in a circle in front of Mr. Tanaka's room.
Mr. Kobayashi hesitated for a moment as he reached to open the door.
He probably didn't want to go near the body.
“You only called into this room, right?”
He asked {n2}, as if reassuring himself.
When she nodded, Mr. Kobayashi turned the knob, resigned.
Cold air poured out.
“Midori?
Are you there?”
All that came back was the howl of the wind.
Mr. Kobayashi took a ski pole and looked into the bathroom.
We watched from the entrance.
Mr. Kobayashi glanced fearfully toward where the body was and came right back.
“...She doesn't seem to be here.”
“Boss!
Hey!”
Toshio called to Mr. Kobayashi from the hallway.
“What is it?”
“Jenny...”
Toshio pointed to the end of the hallway.
The storeroom we had checked earlier.
In front of it, Jenny the black cat was meowing.
Mr. Kobayashi began walking silently.
Jenny noticed us.
She started meowing even louder.
Mr. Kobayashi put his hand on the storeroom doorknob, but for some reason hesitated.
“What's the holdup?
It's just a cat meowin'.{r}{p}We checked there already...”
Mr. Kayama grumbled.
But no one was listening.
Mr. Kobayashi opened the door.
Midori was there.
Her body was folded up and shoved in carelessly, as if stowing a doll or something.
Her eyes were wide open, as if she were surprised to see us.
But those eyes didn't move at all.
“Midori...”
I heard Toshio murmur.
Mr. Kobayashi hurriedly took Midori's hand and checked her pulse.
At last he turned to the rest of us and shook his head without a word.
who would do such a thing...”
Toshio's lips trembled.
“Damn it!
Who would do such a thing...
Damn it, who would do such a thing!”
Toshio started howling like a madman.
Then he clung to Midori's body and sobbed.
“Midori...
Midori...”
...Midori had been beaten to death.
Her head was split open and her long hair was tangled with a huge amount of blood.
“How awful...”
{n2} grabbed my arm, her fingers digging in painfully.
Her face was twisted, and her eyes were brimming with tears, from fear or sorrow, I couldn't tell.
Toshio grabbed the mop handle he'd left on the floor and stood up.
“Come out!
You murderer! Come out!”
Roaring so loudly it seemed his throat might split,
he started down the hallway, pounding on the walls and the guest room doors.
“Toshio,
stop it!”
He shook off Mr. Ko-
bayashi, who tried to stop him, and kept raging.
Maybe hearing the commotion, one of the doors opened and Kanako peeked out.
But when she saw Toshio thrashing like a madman, she hurriedly shut the door.
“Uh, uh...
Mi-
Mi-
Aaaah...!”
Toshio suddenly stopped, knelt in the middle of the hallway, and began to wail.
The victims so far, Mr. Tanaka and Mr. Mikimoto, had been mere passers-by.
Neither had been close to anyone among us.
So until then everyone must have felt, somewhere in their hearts, that it was someone else's problem.
But Midori was different.
To the Kobayashis and Toshio, she was a close coworker.
Judging from Toshio's behavior, she may have been even closer to him.
The dismembered body had produced fear and anxiety.
But Midori's death gave everyone anger and sorrow.
Anger and sorrow strong enough to stand up to fear and anxiety...
“...What?”
“Persuade the girls and bring them down.{r}{p}I'll check on Mr. Mikimoto.”
Without waiting for {n2}'s answer, I opened the door to Mr. Mikimoto's room.
Mr. Mikimoto lay on the bed with a bandage wrapped round and round his head.
With his pale face and closed eyes, he looked dead.
“Mr. Mikimoto...”
“Ugh...
mm.”
He must have been asleep; at my voice he groaned and opened his eyes.
“I think it's safer if we're all together.{r}{p}I'd like you to come downstairs, if you can...{p}can you walk?”
it hurts...”
Even sitting up looked painful.
“Let me lend you a shoulder.”
“Oh, yeah...
thanks.”
Mr. Mikimoto got off the bed and stood.
I think...
I can make it.”
He started walking, swaying.
When I left the room, everyone was waiting.
All three girls had already come out into the hallway.
“To the lounge...
for now.”
I signaled everyone with my eyes.
As I started toward the stairs, Mr. Kobayashi helped me carry Mr. Mikimoto.
“Thanks...”
When I thanked him lightly, Mr. Kobayashi said, looking at the corner of the hallway:
“...Leave those two alone for a while.”
Midori was lying there.
Toshio knelt beside her.
“All right, everyone.
Downstairs...”
At my signal, everyone began to move.
The three of us in front, then {n2}, the girls, the Kayamas, and Kyoko last...
We slowly went down the stairs.
Perhaps five minutes had passed.
Everyone was silent.
Before long, Toshio appeared on the stairs.
He wasn't crying anymore, but his eyes were bright red.
On his back, I could see Midori's head hanging limp.
Toshio came down the stairs slowly, planting each step.
Everyone watched in silence.
No one spoke.
No one tried to help.
No, they couldn't.
There was an atmosphere that made it hard to offer help.
Reaching the bottom of the stairs, Toshio quietly passed in front of us and vanished down the hall.
He had probably gone to take Midori back to her room.
Even after Toshio was gone, no one spoke.
Toshio came back to the lounge sooner than expected.
On his face was a look of some kind of resolve.
I cleared my throat lightly and looked around at everyone.
“Now we're all gathered here.”
Everyone nodded slightly.
“...From now on, please never go off alone.{r}{p}Even to use the restroom, use the first-floor one if you can.{r}{p}If you absolutely must go back to your room,
I'd like you to go in groups of two or more.”
Um...
what on earth happened?”
Keiko asked fearfully.
She seemed not to have been told anything yet.
“Midori was...
just now, someone hit her...”
I couldn't say the rest.
But they seemed to read it from my face; all three gasped, and Aki, as usual, burst into tears.
They pressed even closer together than before, as if trying to stay as far from everyone else as possible.
Mr. Mikimoto's mouth hung open.
“Why on earth...?
Don't tell me she went outside alone?”
He looked as if he couldn't make sense of anything.
she was inside.{r}{p}But...”
want to go back to our room after all!
We don't want to be here!”
Kanako shrieked hysterically.
“No.
We need to stay together.”
“Why?{r}{p}We have nothing to do with this!
Leave us alone!”
They probably thought they'd be safer shutting themselves in, just the three of them.
“That won't do.{r}{p}...
I hate to say this, but I have no choice.{r}{p}...At the time Midori was probably killed, the only people on the second floor were Mr. Mikimoto and you three.”
“What do you...
mean?”
Kanako looked taken aback.
“In other words...
it's possible that you killed Midori.”
It wasn't only the girls and Mr. Mikimoto who looked shocked.
“What are you saying, {n1}!
Do you really think girls could kill Midori?”
{n2}'s accusing tone stabbed at my chest.
But I continued.
One person alone might find it hard.{r}{p}There's the worry the other two would notice.{r}{p}But with all three together...”
Everyone stared at the girls in alarm.
you're kidding! Why would we...
that's awful!”
Keiko looked hurt, and I hurriedly explained.
“Wait a moment.{r}{p}I'm only saying it's a possibility.{r}{p}Like I said before, Mr. Mikimoto had an opportunity to kill Midori too...”
Mr. Mikimoto looked weary.
“I was asleep on sedatives until you came in, remember?{r}{p}And my head is still pounding so bad I can hardly walk...”
But I said:
“That could all be an act.{r}{p}...Don't argue.{r}{p}All I'm saying is that to avoid any more victims, we should all stay together.”
“The killer might be one of us.{r}{p}He might be hiding somewhere in the inn.{r}{p}He might be watching us from the blizzard...”
I rattled off every possibility that came to mind.
“Either way, if we're all together, the killer can't make a move...{r}{p}At least it would be hard for him.”
Everyone fell silent.
They exchanged probing, wary looks with one another.
...I hadn't thought I'd said anything wrong.
But my words had ended up making us suspect one another.
Had I done something unnecessary...?
Was it realistically possible that Mr. Mikimoto or the girls had killed Midori?
The possibility wasn't zero.
When the glass broke, everyone was in the lounge, so neither Mr. Mikimoto nor the girls had a chance to kill Mr. Tanaka.
Besides, even setting opportunity aside, they couldn't have had time to dismember a person.
So Mr. Mikimoto and the girls couldn't have killed Mr. Tanaka.
But just because they hadn't killed Mr. Tanaka
didn't mean they hadn't killed Midori.
Realistically, though, I couldn't think of any reason for these strangers to kill Midori.
What I could think of was...
I remembered what Mr. Kobayashi had said.
“Mr. Kobayashi.
Midori said she wanted to see Mr. Tanaka's room, right? Can you remember exactly what she said?”
Spoken to suddenly, Mr. Kobayashi blinked for a while.
“Uh, yeah...
I think...
'There's something bothering me...'
No, that's not it.
...It was this.
'Something occurred to me, so I want to check Mr. Tanaka's room.'
...I'm pretty sure that's what she said.”
Something occurred to her...
What could it have been?
'Check Mr. Tanaka's room...'
If she said that, it had to be connected to the case.
Maybe she noticed something there and learned the killer's identity?
Then she either confronted the killer or was caught while investigating, and was killed...
That seemed the most natural way to think about it.
Of course, other ways of thinking were possible.
For example, the Kobayashis or Toshio, who knew Midori well, might actually have hated her...
That wasn't unthinkable either.
But for now, we should assume Mr. Tanaka's killer murdered Midori to silence her.
...Among us, only Toshio could have killed Mr. Tanaka.
But Toshio had no opportunity to kill Midori.
Only Mr. Mikimoto and the girls could have killed Midori.
But they couldn't have killed Mr. Tanaka.
“What have you been muttering about all this time?”
{n2} asked uneasily.
“Huh?
Oh, nothing...
I was just sorting out the case...”
“And?”
“It only made me more confused.{r}{p}I can't make heads or tails of it.”
“There's nothing to be confused about.{r}{p}
The killer is someone other than us.{r}{p}A vicious murderer is prowling around nearby.{r}{p}What we need to think about is how to protect ourselves from him.”
At {n2}'s words, Kyoko and Haruko nodded vigorously, as if to say exactly.
“That's right.”
Haruko spoke up for once.
“Suspecting one another won't do any good.{r}{p}Right now we have to trust one another.”
Mr. Kayama chided his wife.
“Haruko.
Pretty talk ain't enough.{r}{p}{n1} is right.{r}{p}We oughta consider every possibility.{r}{p}Otherwise we might not survive till mornin'.”
“But dear...”
“There's no 'but' about it.{r}{p}At times like this, women keep quiet and listen to men.”
Did Mr. Kayama always silence his wife like this?
Or was he just playing the domineering husband in public?
I don't want to think of any of you as murderers, even people I'm close to...{p}though most of you I'm not that close to...{p}But
this inn isn't a very big building...”
Having said that, I glanced at Mr. Kobayashi to see if I'd offended him.
But he didn't seem to mind at all.
“...What I mean is, it's not some giant hotel with blind spots where eyes can't reach.”
“And besides, everything was properly locked.{r}{p}Even a professional burglar couldn't come and go freely in a place like this without anyone noticing, could he?”
Honestly, I don't know which to believe.{r}{p}That an elusive killer is somewhere in the inn.{r}{p}Or that someone who looks like they wouldn't hurt a fly is actually a murderer.
{r}{p}I can't tell.”
I shook my head as I said it.
“You talk like you're the only one not involved.”
Toshio spat out.
what do you mean?”
“Exactly what I said.
You're a suspect too.”
“But I haven't gone to the second floor even once since dinner!{r}{p}There's no way I could have killed Mr. Tanaka!{r}{p}Same with Midori.”
“I didn't see it with my own eyes.{r}{p}Maybe you're just saying that.{r}{p}Your girlfriend's testimony doesn't count either.{r}{p}You can't rely on that.”
“Then let me say something too, Toshio.”
I was getting angrier and angrier.
“Aren't you the one who attacked Mr. Mikimoto?{r}{p}Mr. Mikimoto didn't see the culprit.{r}{p}That means you, who must have been behind him, are the most suspicious, aren't you?”
“No way!{r}{p}The Boss got to where Mr. Mikimoto was lying before I did, you know?{r}{p}Isn't that right, Boss?”
“Huh?
Uh, yeah.
I guess so.”
Mr. Kobayashi gave a vague answer, looking troubled.
It was Toshio who had been walking with Mr. Mikimoto.
I had naturally assumed Toshio had more opportunities to attack him, but...
So was Mr. Kobayashi the suspicious one after all?
Mr. Mikimoto was casting probing looks at both Toshio and Mr. Kobayashi.
It was unexpected.
When I'd seen them, it was Toshio who was helping Mr. Mikimoto up.
So I had assumed Mr. Kobayashi arrived later, but...
So was Mr. Kobayashi the suspicious one after all?
Mr. Mikimoto was casting probing looks at both Toshio and Mr. Kobayashi.
“Stop it!
Please, just stop!”
Kyoko cried out and collapsed in tears.
“Stop hurting each other...”
Regret showed on Mr. Kobayashi's and Toshio's faces.
The same expression was surely on my face, too.
{n2}'s look of contempt was unbearable.
The cuckoo clock sounded.
Without my noticing, it had become eleven-thirty.
The blizzard outside showed no sign of letting up.
“That's right.
The news.{r}{p}I forgot to watch the news.”
Mr. Kayama suddenly cried out.
“...Dear, at a time like this...”
“We can see the weather forecast too.{r}{p}And a change of mood would do us good.”
That opinion might actually be right...
Mr. Kayama picked up the remote without waiting for anyone's answer
and turned on the TV.
Flipping through the channels, he found they were just doing the news headlines.
'...Heavy snow across the country is causing accidents and avalanches in places, but no fatalities have been reported so far.'
No fatalities...
Hearing those words, we instinctively looked up toward the second floor.
'...An industry long questioned for its money-driven culture has been hit by new allegations.
...Now, our top story is the bank robber still on the run.'
'The whereabouts of the man who boldly raided the Shinjuku branch of Sanyu Bank in broad daylight yesterday and made off with roughly 200 million yen in cash remain unknown.{g}
According to witnesses, the robber is a thin man around 165 centimeters tall.
Police are continuing their search with checkpoints in various places for the black coupe believed to have been used in the getaway.'
Now that I thought of it, I'd heard news of a bank robbery on the radio on the drive here.
I'd barely looked at newspapers or TV since, so I hadn't known he was still on the run.
“After a whole day, checkpoints ain't gonna do a thing.{r}{p}By now he's flown off to Southeast Asia or somewhere.”
Mr. Kayama said with a snort.
Maybe he was talking about it on purpose to loosen us up.
I decided to play along.
“...He wouldn't board a plane with two hundred million yen in cash.”
“You never know.{r}{p}Two hundred million ain't that bulky.{r}{p}In new bills, it'd fit in a suitcase easy.”
{n2} joined in the conversation too.
“...Even if he took it, couldn't he use it overseas?{r}{p}If he went to a bank, they'd trace the serial numbers right away...”
“That's an amateur's thinkin'.{r}{p}Yen's still yen, rotten or not.
Some countries like it better than dollars.{r}{p}And there's folks who'll swap it on the black market anywhere.”
“If it were me,”
Toshio cut in too.
Talking probably took his mind off things.

“If it were me, I'd stay in Japan.{r}{p}If you were leaving Japan anyway, wouldn't you go somewhere with cheap prices and live leisurely? You need money because you plan to keep living in Japan, right?
{r}{p}I'd wait out the heat in some country town for a while.”
I thought that might make some sense, but Mr. Kayama shook his head.
“No, no.
In a country town, everybody notices who comes and goes.{r}{p}If you ain't goin' abroad, the city's better.”
“...But it's only human nature not to want to stay near the scene of the crime.”
“It's 'cause they can't hold that urge that they all get caught.{r}{p}Most criminals got no guts, y'know.”
He talked as if he wanted them to show a little more guts.
“In a tourist spot, plenty of outsiders come and go, don't they?”
{n2} said quietly.
“If it's a busy place, sure.
...Like a ski resort in season.”
At Mr. Kayama's words, we all froze.
“Huh?
What's with you all?{r}{p}Lookin' strange.”
Maybe...
no, I'm probably overthinking it.”
I hesitated.
“What?”
never mind.”
“Don't leave it half-said, it's irritatin'.”
I looked around at everyone.
I could tell from some faces that others had thought the same thing.
“All right, but don't laugh.
That Mr. Tanaka who was killed, what if he was the bank robber on the run?”
No one laughed.
Emboldened, I asked Mr. Kobayashi.
“How tall was Mr. Tanaka?”
Mr. Kobayashi thought a moment.
“Pretty tall.
I'd say at least 175.”
175 centimeters...
No good.
The news said the robber was about 165.
Too big a difference.
“...Still, there was something off about him, wasn't there?{r}{p}He had that big ski bag, but he didn't really look like he'd come to ski...”
“Wait a second.”
It was {n2}.
“Normally, a bank robbery needs at least a driver, doesn't it?{r}{p}So maybe Mr. Tanaka was the driver.{r}{p}They had a falling out, and his accomplice killed him.”
“Yeah.
That's possible.{r}{p}Which would make the killer a thin man around 165 centimeters tall.”
Without meaning to, we all looked each other over.
Mr. Kayama was hardly thin.
Mr. Mikimoto and Toshio were too tall.
The closest was...
Mr. Kobayashi.
Mr. Kobayashi was about 165 and thin.
Noticing everyone's eyes on him, Mr. Kobayashi put on a stiff smile.
“Come on.
Enough with the jokes.{r}{p}Just because the news happened to be on, tying it to what happened here is way too far a stretch.”
“Of course it is.
Besides, there's no way Mr. Kobayashi could rob a bank in Tokyo.{r}{p}He's got work here every day.”
Mr. Kayama was right, of course.
It couldn't be Mr. Kobayashi.
Besides, the idea that the victim was a bank robber was itself a hasty leap.
I'd only said it because Mr. Kayama told me it was irritating to leave it half-said.
I hadn't been thinking it seriously.
But {n2} pressed on.
“But I think we might be thinking in the right direction.”
“What do you mean?{r}{P}”
“That Mr. Tanaka didn't look like he'd come to ski at all.{r}{p}He was avoiding people, too. There must have been some shady reason he came to a place like this.”
I'd been thinking that since the moment we found the body.
It had been such an abnormal corpse.
All the more reason I'd wanted to believe it belonged to a world far from our everyday lives.
Neither the killer nor the victim could be ordinary people like us.
The victim, too, must have lived on the shady side of life...
I suppose that wishful thinking had been at work.
But in reality, would a sane person ever think of cutting a body to pieces like that?
I'm the kind of person who looks away when someone gets an injection on TV.
Cutting up a person's body is something I'd refuse no matter how much money they offered.
No matter what the reason...
I suddenly fell into thought.
Did the killer have some reason why Mr. Tanaka's body had to be dismembered?
If there was one...
To hide his identity?
No, in that case he'd cut off the head and hide it.
There'd be no need to cut him up that much, and the head alone would have to be hidden somewhere else.
Question after question swirled in my head and began to take an indistinct shape.
It felt like I could almost grasp it but couldn't, and the frustration made my head itch.
“I never should have come skiing...”
The office girls had started crying again.
All three of them this time.
I want to go home...{p}I didn't do anything wrong...{p}I want to go home...”
Their crying had faded to mere sobbing.
Kyoko began to walk unsteadily.
“Where are you going?{r}{P}”
Mr. Kobayashi asked in surprise.
“...Something to calm everyone down...{p}Maybe some cocoa...”
“No way!{r}{P}
I'm not drinking anything made by someone who might be a murderer!{r}{P}”
Aki cried in a hoarse voice.
But Kyoko showed no sign of being hurt.
“Mrs. Kobayashi can't be the killer.{r}{p}And even if she were, we've eaten and drunk plenty here already, haven't we?{r}{P}{p}If she meant to kill us all, we'd all be dead by now.”
I spoke as quietly as I could, to calm them.
“That's right,
{n1} makes sense.”
“Yes, there's no way Mrs. Kobayashi could be the killer...”
The Kayamas agreed with me.
“...All right.”
Reluctantly, Aki gave in.
“Then I'll go with her.”
{n2} stood up.
“I'm pretty athletic, so if anyone attacks, we'll fight them off together.”
It was necessary so Kyoko wouldn't be alone, but I felt a little uneasy.
“If anything strange happens, shout as loud as you can.”
When I said it, {n2} nodded with a faint smile.
“Okay.
Come ride in on a horse.{r}{p}...A white one.”
Nobody laughed, but I felt the tension ease just a little.
After Kyoko and {n2} went to the kitchen, an eerie silence settled in.
“...Is this all we can do until morning...?”
Toshio murmured.
I nodded and said,

“That's probably best.{r}{p}If the killer isn't one of us, he's some elusive creature who appears and vanishes like a magician.{r}{p}He can come and go from the building and its rooms without anyone noticing.{r}{p}Even if you shut yourself in a room and locked it tight,
could you sleep in peace?{r}{P}”
“...You're right, nobody could feel safe.{r}{p}But think about it.{r}{p}Whoever the killer is, if he meant to kill all of us, would he really use such a roundabout method?{r}{P}{p}If it were me,
I'd have killed a lot more while everyone's guard was still down.”
That was indeed a strange point.
“There's another possibility, isn't there...”
Mr. Mikimoto spoke up, holding his aching head.
“That the aim is to make the survivors taste fear...”
“To make us taste fear...?{r}{P}{p}What do you mean?”
I asked back.
“I mean the killer holds a serious grudge against all of us, or one of us, and simply killing isn't enough.{r}{p}So like a cat toying with a mouse, he scares us first and kills us at the end...
.{r}{p}Maybe that's what he intends.”
Scare us first, then kill us...
If that was true, how deep did that grudge run?
Was there anyone among us who could earn that kind of hatred?
“Then...
does that mean everyone except the one he hates is safe?{r}{P}”
Keiko asked Mr. Mikimoto with pleading eyes.
“...Who knows.{r}{p}I was hit on the head, but strangely I didn't feel any intent to kill.{r}{p}Of course, he may simply not have had time to finish me off because someone came...
.{r}{p}Maybe he has no intention of killing unrelated people.”
“Don't talk nonsense!{r}{P}{p}What about Midori...? What about her?!{r}{P}{p}The killer has already killed an unrelated person!”
Toshio said, his anger plain.
“...How do you know she was unrelated?{r}{P}”
When Mr. Mikimoto asked back quietly, Toshio's face went bright red and he shouted even louder.
“What do you mean?!{r}{P}
She...
Midori...!{r}{P}”
His voice choked.
“...I'm sorry.
I didn't mean to speak ill of her.{r}{p}It's just that, putting everything together, it seems to me the killer only kills when he absolutely has to...”
What reason could there be...
for Midori to have to be killed...”
While Mr. Mikimoto spoke, Toshio's anger seemed to turn into sorrow.
The tears that had once dried welled up again.
Whether from sympathy or fear, even the girls and Haruko had tears in their eyes.
Had Toshio loved her...?
I, who hardly knew the two of them, couldn't tell.
...Right, all of this could be an act.
He might have killed Midori and be pretending to have loved her so as not to be suspected.
I was thoroughly disgusted with myself for thinking such things.
Why, why did we have to suspect one another like this?
I couldn't even sympathize honestly with a man grieving for the person he loved.
But it was all because we didn't know the killer's identity.
Was it someone we didn't know?{r}{P}
Or was he among us?{r}{P}
Until even that was clear, we couldn't make a move.
...Come to think of it.
Something in Mr. Mikimoto's earlier words bothered me.
'...It seems to me the killer only kills when he absolutely has to...'
She was killed because the killer absolutely had to...
I had surely thought of this once before.
Why was Midori killed?
Had she seen something?
Had she just happened to run into the killer?
I realized what I should have done first.
Search Mr. Tanaka's room thoroughly.
Midori had said she was going to that room, and she was killed.
The clue had to be in that room.
Ideally I'd examine it carefully alone.
But having told everyone nobody should be left alone, I could hardly do that now.
Of course I knew being alone was dangerous.
But taking someone who might be the killer into the room would be even more dangerous.
Then, with whom...?
The answer came at once.
With {n2}, I could search without worry.
Before long, {n2} came back with Kyoko, carrying a tray loaded with cups.
“Sorry to keep you waiting.”
{n2} was putting on the brightest voice she could manage.
It felt strange, knowing Midori had done the very same thing not long ago.
Someone who'd been perfectly fine just a few hours earlier was now cold...
Steaming hot cocoa was handed out to everyone.
The girls waited until the others had taken a sip before they began drinking.
The warm, sweet cocoa seemed to have a strongly calming effect.
It felt as if the weariness of my heart and body, everything, was melting away.
Once we'd all caught our breath and seemed a little calmer, I said to {n2}.
“...Could you come with me for a bit?”
“Where?{r}{P}”
“...I'm going to search Mr. Tanaka's room.”
Everyone turned to look at me with a start.
“What do you hope to find by that?{r}{P}”
Mr. Kobayashi asked.
“Midori was trying to go to that room before she was killed.{r}{p}{p}Right?{r}{P}”
“Yes,
that's true, but...{r}{p}What does that have to do with...”
“She was probably trying to look into the truth of the case.{r}{p}And she got too close to it, so she was killed.{r}{p}So I think what we should do is search that room thoroughly.”
“You're going to do it?{r}{P}”
Toshio cut in, narrowing his eyes.
“Yes.”
“What guarantee is there that you're not the killer and won't destroy the evidence?{r}{P}”
“That's...”
“There isn't one, is there?{r}{P}”
“But I don't intend to go in alone.
I'll be with {n2}.”
“That's the point!{r}{P}
There's no guarantee she isn't your accomplice, either.”
“...Then let's go, the three of us.{r}{p}You can't object to that, can you?{r}{P}{p}Toshio, please pick one more person.”
“What, I'm not good enough?{r}{P}”
Toshio's eyebrows shot up.
If he was the killer, he might destroy the evidence.
